newsitem.title: UK: Arafat thanks Blair for support on peace process.
newsitem.headline: Arafat thanks Blair for support on peace process.

text.p: Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat on Monday thanked Britain for its moral and political support in backing efforts to move the Middle East peace process out of what he described as its current "impasse".

Speaking after a 50-minute meeting with Prime Minister Tony Blair at his London office, Arafat told reporters: "I thanked him for what he is doing with all his capability to protect the peace process."

British diplomatic sources said Blair and Foreign Office minister Derek Fatchett who held an earlier meeting with Arafat had backed his call for a halt to Jewish settlement in the occupied territories.
But they had told the Palestinian leader he must resume full security cooperation with Israeli forces if peace talks with Israel are to be revived.

Formal peace talks have been frozen since Israel broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem four months ago. Arafat said he had discussed with Blair "the impasse of the peace talks as a result of the measures taken by Israel".
Diplomats said Britain is preparing to take a more central role on the issue when it takes over the rotating presidency of the European Union in the first half of next year.
London believes the EU should play a greater diplomatic role in the Middle East given its economic importance to the region, they said.
Hours before meeting Arafat, Blair held a brief meeting with Ehur Barak, the leader of Israel's Labour opposition. His aides said the two meetings were not linked.
